protocol.hipengine: scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py, greedy, bf16 KV, execution profile default
protocol.prompt: both engines receive the same prompt ids from exact_prompt_ids; llama.cpp's own tokenizer round-trips them (text_probe.llama_tokens == prompt_tokens at both lengths), so the two are scored on identical input

findings: The objective's premise that prefill is about 30x off llama.cpp is out of date on this platform: the measured gap is 3.54x at 512/128 and 5.14x at 1024/128. The int8 expert gate/up route becoming the default is part of what closed it - this run reports 257.2 tok/s at 512/128 against the 154.3 tok/s the campaign changelog recorded for this same box before that change.

The gap widens with prompt length, and it widens from opposite directions: hipEngine falls from 257.2 to 230.0 tok/s going from 512 to 1024 prompt tokens while llama.cpp rises from 909.3 to 1183.1. A fixed per-prefill cost amortising over more tokens explains llama.cpp rising; hipEngine falling points at work that grows with length, which is the campaign's first open item - the 5 global layers at head_dim 512 have no tiled kernel, so past the window later blocks fall back to the slow one.

Decode is flat across both lengths and both engines, at 21.06/19.95 for hipEngine against 36.03/33.66 for llama.cpp. The objective's 2x decode target (about 42 tok/s) is therefore above llama.cpp's own number here, not merely a match to it.
limits: One box, one artifact, one prompt corpus (the campaign's exact-token chain). These are baselines for driving the next change, not promotion evidence.
The peak device memory hipEngine holds is 24.46 GB. The gfx1100 branch's stride change (e202b4080, 32.35 -> 23.58 GB) is not in this branch.
